title: SMI 2025 Conference Highlights: Neural Interfaces and Beyond
excerpt: Notes from the Summer Meeting on Neural Interfaces — poster sessions, unexpected conversations, and the state of the field.
body: Spent three days at SMI 2025 (Summer Meeting on Interfaces). Here's what stuck with me.
The opening keynote on in-vivo neural dust was eye-opening. The speaker demonstrated a 0.5mm3 wireless recording system that could theoretically run for years on a single microbattery.
We're not building devices for the lab anymore. We're building devices for a lifetime.
• Stretchable optogenetics — fiber optics that stretch with the brain
• AI-assisted spike sorting — real-time denoising at the edge
• Organ-on-chip integration — the buzz is real, the results are mixed
A recurring theme: organoid interfaces are hard. Not impossible, just hard. Multiple groups showed results similar to ours — consistent coupling is the bottleneck.

Industry Trend
Three companies at the expo were commercializing organoid screening platforms. The field is maturing.

The best conversations happened over coffee. A materials scientist from Tokyo mentioned using EGaIn (eutectic gallium-indium) for soft contacts — liquid metal that conforms without stiffness. I need to try this.
• Reach out to the AI spike sorting team for collaboration
If you attended, I'd love to compare notes. Drop me a message.
